solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mix juice and yellow colouring

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them together, so the letters of the two words beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, part of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: blend some juice to get a yellow tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: 'Mix' shuffles JUICE and AND together.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice is the yellowing of skin and eyes, a yellow discolouration of the body.

clue.text: Piece of furniture is tops in school of fine art

indicators.note: the tops of words in a down clue are their first letters, so we take the initial of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An art college boasts that its best furniture design is its pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, an item of household furniture.

clue.text: For example limiting iron temperature gives freedom from danger

indicators.note: limiting means bounding or enclosing, so the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, as in 'a fruit, say'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A rule about keeping an iron's heat down to stay out of harm's way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it introduces an illustration, but it stands for the word used before an example, as in 'fruit, say, apples'.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is the condition of being protected from harm or risk.

clue.text: Low voice, alien for hound

parts.note: bass is the lowest male singing voice
ET, the extraterrestrial of the Spielberg film, is a standard alien

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced singer swapped for a dog, sounding like a strange trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog, a type of hound.

clue.text: Caught husband aboard earlier boat

indicators.note: aboard means on or within, so the two letters go inside the word for earlier

parts.note: sooner means earlier, at a previous time
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wife's husband was caught getting onto an earlier boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, a type of boat.

clue.text: Pleased with good boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A parent is happy with a well-behaved son.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a synonym of pleased, meaning happy about something.

clue.text: Big picture: someone childless is neither a ____

parts.note: a person with no children is not a parent of either sex, so the blank wants the homely words for father and mother joined by the word that follows neither

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank riddle: what is a childless person not?
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is completed by the phrase PA NOR A MA, which run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, all-round view, so figuratively the overall perspective or broad overview.

clue.text: Part of collection put back in small room

indicators.note: put back means the letters are returned in the opposite direction, read backwards
part of a word means a run of its letters is taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Returning one item from a collection to a little storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses LLEC, the letters lifted from 'collection' by 'Part of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or a monastery.

clue.text: Maybe to vape is popular and healthy

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A claim that vaping is fashionable and good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: vaping is one way to breathe in.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaping draws vapour into the lungs, one instance of breathing in.

clue.text: Second promise to produce weapon

parts.note: to give your word is to make a promise

explanation.surface: A second pledge yields arms, as in a knight's vow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed weapon with a long metal blade and a hilt.

clue.text: Occasion to forget married bond

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the word for occasion

parts.note: a time is an occasion, as in 'the last time we met'

explanation.surface: An occasion when someone forgets the bond of their marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a link or connection, as in family ties, so a bond.

clue.text: One half of sermon getting into goodness and suffering

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so these letters are placed inside the exclamation

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness!'
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word gives three letters; here the front half is taken

explanation.surface: A preacher's long sermon brings both piety and pain to the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' is the mild exclamation, as in 'my, how you've grown', not virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery is great distress or unhappiness, a state of suffering.

clue.text: Snarl up net that has twisted corner

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: an angle is a corner, where two lines meet

explanation.surface: A fisherman's net has got tangled at one corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges the three letters of 'net' to give the opening of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to snarl up or knot together, as with fishing line.

clue.text: Disorderly punk at booze a lot

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly punk rocker drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank up is informal for drinking a great deal of alcohol, getting drunk.

clue.text: Everything in French, one current poem

parts.note: un is French for one
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
verse is poetry, a poem

explanation.surface: A description of a single French poem, mentioning electricity in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all existing matter and space, the whole of everything.

clue.text: Leave small portion around to dine on

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for small portion goes either side of the eating word

parts.note: a bit is a small portion
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave a small portion of food for someone to eat later.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for go away or depart, an order to leave.

clue.text: Prize public house within ancient city

indicators.note: within means inside, so the pub abbreviation sits inside the city

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub, seen on British maps

explanation.surface: A pub in a historic city awards a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or award given as a prize for a win.

clue.text: Unhealthy announcement of further offer

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the answer is the sound of the next phrase

parts.note: more means further, additional; a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: At an auction, a bidder announces a higher offer that seems unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid means of disease, in medical use, so diseased or unhealthy; also unwholesome in interest.

clue.text: Recall top couples in Melton Mowbray and Rydal

indicators.note: a couple is two, and the top in a down clue is the start, so the first two letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Remembering a trip to two English towns known to the rambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top couples in' takes the first two letters of each word: ME, MO, RY. Melton Mowbray is an English market town famed for pork pies; Rydal is a Lake District village.
explanation.definitionFit: Recall as a noun is the power of remembering, so memory.

clue.text: Feel bad about Parisian street

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Regretting something done on a street in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is both a verb of regret and the French noun for a road in town.

clue.text: Staff turn tropical fruit

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Employees take turns at a fruit stall in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as a noun, but it is the verb MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a sweet, fleshy stone fruit grown in hot climates.

clue.text: Gospel writer is one suitable for swindling

definitions.meaning: One of the four evangelists who wrote a Gospel
a con artist's target, someone easily cheated

explanation.surface: A cynic's suggestion that an evangelist is easy to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Mark wrote the second Gospel; in slang a mark is a gullible victim of a con.

clue.text: Perhaps Busby and Queen are important

parts.note: Sir Matt Busby, the long-serving Manchester United football manager, is one Matt
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A claim that a football manager and a monarch are significant figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To matter is to be important or significant, as in 'details matter'.

clue.text: Work up to time without good health

parts.note: ill means not in good health

explanation.surface: Someone works until a set time despite being unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to' is a bonus definition: till also means until.
explanation.definitionFit: To till is to work the soil, cultivating land for crops.

clue.text: Spoken for, Val needing no introductions

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their first letters, so each word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone already engaged to Val needs no introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken for' looks like one phrase meaning engaged, but 'Spoken' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken aloud rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Innocuous, not at all alluring but not cold

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so a letter is removed from the word before

parts.note: charmless means without charm, not alluring at all
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A description of something dull and unappealing but at least not chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless means causing no harm, a plain synonym for innocuous.
